definitions.explanation: A child who has lost one or both parents, especially one who has no guardian.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{孤児|こじ}になった。
examples.english: I became an orphan because of the war.

examples.japanese: {孤児|こじ}{院|いん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{育|そだ}った→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧。
examples.english: I grew up in an orphanage.

examples.japanese: ⟦{震災|しんさい}→震災：14610_shinsai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{孤児|こじ}となり、⟦{支援|しえん}→支援：07778_shien⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Many children were orphaned by the earthquake disaster, and support is needed.

notes:
The standard term for an orphan in Japanese. Also read as みなしご, which is a more literary and emotional reading of the same kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {孤児|こじ}{院|いん} — orphanage
- ⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧{孤児|こじ} — war orphan
- {孤児|こじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ — to become an orphan
- {孤児|こじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}き{取|と}る→引き取る：06164_hikitoru⟧ — to take in an orphan

PRONUNCIATION:
- こじ — the standard modern reading, used in news and formal contexts
- みなしご — a native Japanese reading, more literary and emotional

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {遺児|いじ} — bereaved child (specifically a child who lost parents to disaster or accident; often used in compound ⟦{交通|こうつう}→交通：01584_koutsuu⟧{遺児|いじ}, traffic orphan)
